candidate.answerReason: George normally has 20 minutes for the trip. The first half-mile takes 15 minutes today, leaving 5 minutes to cover the remaining half-mile, which requires 6 miles per hour.

methods.label: Find the remaining travel time
methods.explanation:
Leaving at the usual time gives George the same total travel time as on other days. At \(3\) miles per hour, each mile takes
\[
60\div3=20\text{ minutes}.
\]

At today's slower speed of \(2\) miles per hour, a full mile would take \(60\div2=30\) minutes. The first half-mile therefore takes \(15\) minutes, leaving \(20-15=5\) minutes before school begins.

Covering half a mile in \(5\) minutes means covering one mile in \(10\) minutes at the same speed. That is \(6\) miles in \(60\) minutes, so George must run at \(6\) miles per hour, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Working in minutes reduces the problem to elementary rate reasoning, division, and subtraction.
